library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Goncalves_2017_primaquine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Goncalves_2017_primaquine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.02590-16>

Goncalves 2017 is the first primaquine (PQ) pharmacokinetic study in African
children. A semi-physiological population model describes PQ and its main
plasma metabolite carboxyprimaquine (CPQ) jointly. The final model has three
features beyond allometric weight scaling: relative bioavailability that
matures with age, a CYP2D6 intrinsic clearance proportional to the
genotype-derived CYP2D6 activity score (AS), and a well-stirred liver in which
monoamine oxidase (MAO) forms CPQ. Only the final model has reported
estimates (Table 2), so it is the one packaged here. The Lee 2021 primaquine
model in this library (`Lee_2021_primaquine`) uses the same liver structure in
Korean adults.

# Population

Forty afebrile, G6PD-normal children aged 2-14 years in Balonghin, Burkina
Faso, 37 with asymptomatic *P. falciparum* parasitaemia, received a single
primaquine dose of 0.25 mg/kg (n = 20) or 0.40 mg/kg (n = 20) with the fifth
dose of a six-dose artemether-lumefantrine course (Methods; Table 1). The dose
was given as a 1 mg/mL solution of a crushed 15 mg tablet. Median (IQR) age was
8 (6-10) and 10 (6.5-12) years, weight 19.8 (16.2-26.3) and 24.9
(15.9-31.6) kg and height 118 (104-133.5) and 129 (104-144.5) cm in the two
arms; 55% and 60% were female. Of the 36 children genotyped, one was a CYP2D6
poor metabolizer (AS 0), ten intermediate (AS 0.5 or 1.0), 22 extensive
(AS 1.5 or 2.0) and three ultrarapid (AS 3.0); the four without a genotype
were set to AS 1.5. Two children were excluded from the PK analysis for
inadequate sample volume, leaving 38 children and seven samples each (one
pre-dose, four in 0-12 h, two in 24-72 h). The LC-MS assay had an LLOQ of
4 ng/mL; BLQ samples were handled with Beal's M6 method.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Goncalves_2017_primaquine")()$population`.

# Model structure

```{r structure, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tribble(
    ~`Figure 2 rate constant`, ~Definition, ~`Model code`,
    "k12, k23, k34", "3 / MAT", "ktr * depot, ktr * transit1, ktr * transit2",
    "k46", "QH (1 - EH) / VL", "qh * (1 - eh) * liver / vliver",
    "k64", "QH / VPQ", "qh * central / vc",
    "k40", "CLH,CYP2D6 / VL", "clh_cyp2d6 * liver / vliver (lost)",
    "k45", "CLH,MAO / VL", "mw_ratio * clh_mao * liver / vliver (forms CPQ)",
    "k50", "CLCPQ / VCPQ", "cl_cpq * central_cpq / vc_cpq"
  ),
  caption = "Figure 2 of Goncalves 2017 and its encoding."
)
```

* **Absorption.** Depot and two transit compartments at `ktr = (n + 1) / MAT`
  with `n = 2` (Methods; Figure 2 gives `k12 = k23 = k34 = 3/MAT`), feeding
  the liver.
* **Bioavailability.** `F = AGE / (AGE + F50)` (Results), applied to the dose.
* **Well-stirred liver.** `EH = CLint / (QH + CLint)` with `CLint` the sum of
  the MAO and CYP2D6 intrinsic clearances; each hepatic clearance is
  `CLH = EH * QH` apportioned by the pathway's share of `CLint` (Methods).
  Total outflow from the liver is therefore `QH`: `QH (1 - EH)` returns to
  plasma, and `QH * EH` is metabolised.
* **CYP2D6.** `CLint,CYP2D6,i = AS * CLint,CYP2D6,pop` (Methods).
* **Scaling.** Every flow and clearance (QH, both intrinsic clearances,
  CLCPQ) scales as `(WT/70)^0.75` and every volume (VPQ, VCPQ) as
  `(WT/70)^1` (Methods; Table 2 footnote). QH is 49.5 L/h at 70 kg.
* **Liver volume.** VL comes from weight and height through body surface area
  (Methods, citing Johnson 2005): `VL (L) = 0.722 * BSA^1.176`.
* **Units.** The authors fitted in molar units. The packaged model doses in mg
  of PQ base and reports ng/mL, so the MAO flux is multiplied by the
  CPQ:PQ molecular-weight ratio 274.32 / 259.35.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Goncalves_2017_primaquine.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lmat` | log(0.706) h | Table 2, mean absorption time |
| `lvc` | log(127) L at 70 kg | Table 2, VPQ |
| `lvc_cpq` | log(21.7) L at 70 kg | Table 2, VCPQ |
| `lclint_mao` | log(7.35) L/h at 70 kg | Table 2, CLint,MAO |
| `lclint_cyp2d6` | log(6.70) L/h at 70 kg per unit AS | Table 2, CLint,CYP2D6,pop |
| `lcl_cpq` | log(1.50) L/h at 70 kg | Table 2, CLCPQ |
| `age50_fdepot` | 4.27 years | Table 2, F50; Results |
| `lqh` | fixed log(49.5) L/h at 70 kg | Methods |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | fixed 0.75, 1 | Methods; Table 2 footnote |
| `etalvc` | log(1 + 0.829^2) | Table 2, VPQ IIV 82.9% |
| `etalclint_mao` | log(1 + 0.653^2) | Table 2, CLint,MAO IIV 65.3% |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.327, fixed 2 ng/mL | Table 2, residual error PQ |
| `propSd_cpq`, `addSd_cpq` | 0.452, fixed 2 ng/mL | Table 2, residual error CPQ |
| Transit absorption | `ktr = 3 / MAT` | Methods; Figure 2 |
| `F` maturation | `AGE / (AGE + F50)` | Results, Pharmacokinetics |
| Well-stirred liver, `EH`, `CLH` | as above | Methods; Figure 2 |
| CYP2D6 effect | `AS * CLint,CYP2D6,pop` | Methods |
| Liver volume | `0.722 * BSA^1.176` | Methods, ref. 44 (Johnson 2005 abstract) |
| BSA | DuBois (< 15 kg) / Haycock (>= 15 kg) | not printed; see Assumptions |
| Molar PQ to CPQ conversion | 274.32 / 259.35 | Methods (molar fit); molecular formulas |

# Deterministic checks

```{r mod}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Goncalves_2017_primaquine"))
# No cl/vc pair is defined, so rxode2 keeps the explicit ODEs.
stopifnot(is.null(mod$linCmt))
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Two declared endpoints (Cc, Cc_cpq): observation rows nominate dvid = 1 on
# the central state and both observables come back as columns.
make_events <- function(cov, dose_mgkg, obs_times) {
  dose_rows <- cov |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_mgkg * WT, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(cov, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
```

## Closed-form exposure

Every absorbed molecule enters the well-stirred liver, so the PQ AUC after a
single dose is `F * Dose / CLint` and the CPQ AUC is
`F * Dose * (CLint,MAO / CLint) * (274.32 / 259.35) / CLCPQ`, whatever the
volumes. Solving the typical-value model to 400 h checks the ODE encoding
against both identities.

```{r closed-form}
cf_cov <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  AGE = c(2, 8, 14, 14),
  WT = c(12, 20, 40, 40),
  HT = c(85, 118, 151, 151),
  CYP2D6 = c(1, 1.5, 0, 3)
)
ev_cf <- make_events(cf_cov, 0.25, sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.01), seq(12, 400, by = 0.1)))))
sim_cf <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_cf,
  returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
))
closed <- sim_cf |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(auc_pq = trap(time, Cc), auc_cpq = trap(time, Cc_cpq), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(cf_cov, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    f = AGE / (AGE + 4.27),
    clint_mao = 7.35 * (WT / 70)^0.75,
    clint = clint_mao + CYP2D6 * 6.70 * (WT / 70)^0.75,
    cl_cpq = 1.50 * (WT / 70)^0.75,
    auc_pq_exact = 1000 * f * 0.25 * WT / clint,
    auc_cpq_exact = 1000 * f * 0.25 * WT * (clint_mao / clint) * (274.32 / 259.35) / cl_cpq
  )
knitr::kable(
  closed |>
    select(AGE, WT, CYP2D6, auc_pq, auc_pq_exact, auc_cpq, auc_cpq_exact) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Age (y)" = AGE, "WT (kg)" = WT, "AS" = CYP2D6,
      "PQ AUC (ODE)" = auc_pq, "PQ closed form" = auc_pq_exact,
      "CPQ AUC (ODE)" = auc_cpq, "CPQ closed form" = auc_cpq_exact
    ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Typical-value AUC0-400 (ng*h/mL) after 0.25 mg/kg against the closed forms."
)
# Same parameters on both sides; the residual is trapezoid error plus the
# fraction of CPQ AUC beyond 400 h (half-life at most ~10 h, so negligible).
stopifnot(
  all(abs(closed$auc_pq / closed$auc_pq_exact - 1) < 0.002),
  all(abs(closed$auc_cpq / closed$auc_cpq_exact - 1) < 0.002)
)
```

## Replication of Figure 5

Figure 5 shows model-derived typical profiles after 0.25 mg/kg: a 2-year-old
of 12 kg and a 14-year-old of 40 kg with AS 1.0 (panels A and B), and four
14-year-olds with AS 0, 1, 2 and 3 (panels C and D). The maintainers digitised
the curves from the published bitmap against the axis tick marks (to about
+/- 1 ng/mL for PQ and +/- 2 ng/mL for CPQ). Figure 5 gives no heights; 85 cm
and 151 cm are used, and the liver-volume check below shows height does not
matter.

```{r fig5-digitised}
fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~panel, ~child, ~AGE, ~WT, ~HT, ~CYP2D6, ~analyte, ~time, ~digitised,
  "A", "2 y, AS 1", 2, 12, 85, 1, "PQ", NA, 28.6,
  "A", "2 y, AS 1", 2, 12, 85, 1, "PQ", 4, 21.4,
  "A", "2 y, AS 1", 2, 12, 85, 1, "PQ", 8, 12.4,
  "B", "2 y, AS 1", 2, 12, 85, 1, "CPQ", NA, 59.4,
  "B", "2 y, AS 1", 2, 12, 85, 1, "CPQ", 4, 54.6,
  "B", "2 y, AS 1", 2, 12, 85, 1, "CPQ", 20, 32.7,
  "A", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "PQ", NA, 71.9,
  "A", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "PQ", 4, 57.8,
  "A", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "PQ", 8, 38.9,
  "A", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "PQ", 12, 25.9,
  "A", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "PQ", 20, 11.9,
  "B", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "CPQ", NA, 142.9,
  "B", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "CPQ", 4, 121.6,
  "B", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "CPQ", 12, 139.4,
  "B", "14 y, AS 1", 14, 40, 151, 1, "CPQ", 20, 107.4,
  "C", "14 y, AS 0", 14, 40, 151, 0, "PQ", NA, 83.8,
  "C", "14 y, AS 0", 14, 40, 151, 0, "PQ", 8, 60.0,
  "C", "14 y, AS 0", 14, 40, 151, 0, "PQ", 20, 30.2,
  "D", "14 y, AS 0", 14, 40, 151, 0, "CPQ", NA, 204.5,
  "D", "14 y, AS 0", 14, 40, 151, 0, "CPQ", 4, 148.9,
  "D", "14 y, AS 0", 14, 40, 151, 0, "CPQ", 20, 187.3,
  "C", "14 y, AS 2", 14, 40, 151, 2, "PQ", NA, 64.4,
  "C", "14 y, AS 2", 14, 40, 151, 2, "PQ", 8, 30.2,
  "C", "14 y, AS 2", 14, 40, 151, 2, "PQ", 12, 18.4,
  "D", "14 y, AS 2", 14, 40, 151, 2, "CPQ", NA, 115.5,
  "D", "14 y, AS 2", 14, 40, 151, 2, "CPQ", 20, 76.3,
  "C", "14 y, AS 3", 14, 40, 151, 3, "PQ", NA, 59.7,
  "C", "14 y, AS 3", 14, 40, 151, 3, "PQ", 8, 24.9,
  "C", "14 y, AS 3", 14, 40, 151, 3, "PQ", 12, 13.8,
  "D", "14 y, AS 3", 14, 40, 151, 3, "CPQ", NA, 100.8,
  "D", "14 y, AS 3", 14, 40, 151, 3, "CPQ", 20, 60.9
)

fig5_cov <- fig5 |>
  distinct(child, AGE, WT, HT, CYP2D6) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
ev5 <- make_events(fig5_cov |> select(id, AGE, WT, HT, CYP2D6), 0.25, seq(0, 24, by = 0.05))
sim5 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev5, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  left_join(fig5_cov |> select(id, child), by = "id")

sim5_long <- sim5 |>
  select(child, time, PQ = Cc, CPQ = Cc_cpq) |>
  pivot_longer(c(PQ, CPQ), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc")
model_at <- function(ch, an, tt) {
  s <- sim5_long[sim5_long$child == ch & sim5_long$analyte == an, ]
  if (is.na(tt)) max(s$conc) else s$conc[which.min(abs(s$time - tt))]
}
fig5_cmp <- fig5 |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(model = model_at(child, analyte, time)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    feature = ifelse(is.na(time), "peak", paste0(time, " h")),
    pct_diff = 100 * (model / digitised - 1)
  )
knitr::kable(
  fig5_cmp |>
    select(panel, child, analyte, feature, digitised, model, pct_diff) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Panel" = panel, "Child" = child, "Analyte" = analyte, "Feature" = feature,
      "Figure 5 (ng/mL)" = digitised, "Model (ng/mL)" = model, "% diff" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Typical-value model against the digitised Figure 5 curves."
)
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Goncalves 2017: typical PQ and CPQ profiles after 0.25 mg/kg. Lines are the packaged model; points are digitised from the published figure."}
ggplot(sim5_long, aes(time, conc, colour = child)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = fig5_cmp |> filter(!is.na(time)),
    aes(time, digitised, colour = child), inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(analyte, levels = c("PQ", "CPQ")), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The 2-year-old, the AS 0 and the AS 1 curves reproduce Figure 5 to within the
digitising error, which exercises the age-maturation of F, the allometric
scaling of QH and the clearances, the MAO-to-CPQ molar conversion and the
well-stirred liver. The AS 2 and AS 3 curves of the model lie below the
published ones, by up to 18% at the late PQ points, where the
concentrations are small. Each published curve matches a single
model curve at an *effective* activity score: about 1.82 for the curve
labelled AS 2 and about 2.47 for AS 3, with PQ peak, CPQ peak, PQ at 12 h and
CPQ at 20 h all agreeing on the same value. The figure therefore behaves as if
the CYP2D6 clearance rose less than proportionally above AS 1. The Methods
state the linear form `CLint,CYP2D6,i = AS * CLint,CYP2D6,pop` explicitly, and
the packaged model follows the printed equation; see Assumptions.

```{r fig5-gates}
exact <- fig5_cmp |> filter(CYP2D6 <= 1)
high_as <- fig5_cmp |> filter(CYP2D6 >= 2)
stopifnot(
  # Age, weight, AS 0 and AS 1: a mis-transcribed F50, clearance, volume,
  # QH scaling or molar ratio moves these by tens of percent.
  all(abs(exact$pct_diff[exact$digitised >= 10]) < 5),
  all(abs(exact$pct_diff[exact$digitised < 10] / 100 * exact$digitised[exact$digitised < 10]) < 1),
  # AS 2-3: the model is BELOW the figure (the documented linear-AS
  # deviation), and not by more than the effective-AS offset explains.
  all(high_as$pct_diff < 0),
  all(high_as$pct_diff > -30)
)
```

## Liver volume does not affect the plasma profiles

The paper does not print the BSA formula behind its liver volume. The liver
residence time `VL / QH` is about two minutes, so the volume cannot shape the
plasma profiles. Scaling VL by 0.5 and 2 (through height, the only route by
which it enters) confirms this.

```{r vl-sensitivity}
vl_cov <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:3, AGE = 14, WT = 40, HT = c(151, 151, 151), CYP2D6 = 1)
# HT^(0.3964 * 1.176) is the height dependence of VL for WT >= 15 kg; solve for
# the heights that halve and double VL.
vl_cov$HT <- 151 * c(1, 0.5, 2)^(1 / (0.3964 * 1.176))
ev_vl <- make_events(vl_cov, 0.25, seq(0, 48, by = 0.05))
sim_vl <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_vl, returnType = "data.frame"))
vl_sum <- sim_vl |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cmax_pq = max(Cc), cmax_cpq = max(Cc_cpq), .groups = "drop")
vl_sum$vl_multiplier <- c(1, 0.5, 2)
knitr::kable(vl_sum |>
  select(vl_multiplier, cmax_pq, cmax_cpq) |>
  dplyr::rename("VL multiplier" = vl_multiplier, "PQ Cmax" = cmax_pq, "CPQ Cmax" = cmax_cpq),
digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(vl_sum$cmax_pq / vl_sum$cmax_pq[1] - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(vl_sum$cmax_cpq / vl_sum$cmax_cpq[1] - 1) < 0.02)
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. Two arms of 200 virtual children reproduce
Table 1:

* Age is normal, redrawn until it falls in the studied 2-14 years. The mean
  and SD (8.2 and 3 years in the 0.25 mg/kg arm, 10.5 and 3.5 years in the
  0.40 mg/kg arm) are chosen to approximate the Table 1 medians (8 and 10
  years) and IQRs; the realised medians and IQRs are tabulated below.
* Weight follows the exponential age trend through the two Table 1 medians
  (19.8 kg at 8 years and 24.9 kg at 10 years), with 15% log-normal scatter.
* Height follows the linear trend through the Table 1 medians (118 cm at 8
  years, 129 cm at 10 years), with 6 cm scatter.
* The CYP2D6 activity score is drawn from the genotyped frequencies. The
  paper splits the intermediate (AS 0.5 or 1.0) and extensive (AS 1.5 or 2.0)
  groups no further, so each group is split evenly, and the four children
  without a genotype are added at AS 1.5. This gives AS 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2
  and 3 in proportions 1:5:5:15:11:3 of 40.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20170517)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20170517)
n_arm <- 200
draw_age <- function(n, mean, sd) {
  age <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  while (any(bad <- age < 2 | age > 14)) age[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
  age
}
make_arm <- function(n, arm, dose_mgkg, age_mean, age_sd, id_offset) {
  age <- draw_age(n, age_mean, age_sd)
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    dose_mgkg = dose_mgkg,
    AGE = age,
    WT = 19.8 * exp(log(24.9 / 19.8) / 2 * (age - 8)) * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.15)),
    HT = 118 + 5.5 * (age - 8) + rnorm(n, 0, 6),
    CYP2D6 = sample(c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(1, 5, 5, 15, 11, 3))
  )
}
cohort <- bind_rows(
  make_arm(n_arm, "0.25 mg/kg", 0.25, 8.2, 3, 0L),
  make_arm(n_arm, "0.40 mg/kg", 0.40, 10.5, 3.5, n_arm)
)
cohort |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    age = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median(AGE), quantile(AGE, 0.25), quantile(AGE, 0.75)),
    wt = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f-%.1f)", median(WT), quantile(WT, 0.25), quantile(WT, 0.75)),
    ht = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(HT), quantile(HT, 0.25), quantile(HT, 0.75)),
    as_mean = mean(CYP2D6)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "N" = n, "Age, y" = age, "Weight, kg" = wt,
    "Height, cm" = ht, "Mean AS" = as_mean
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual cohort, median (IQR); compare Table 1.")
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.1), seq(4, 24, by = 0.5), seq(24, 168, by = 2))))
ev <- bind_rows(
  make_events(cohort |> filter(arm == "0.25 mg/kg") |> select(id, AGE, WT, HT, CYP2D6), 0.25, obs_times),
  make_events(cohort |> filter(arm == "0.40 mg/kg") |> select(id, AGE, WT, HT, CYP2D6), 0.40, obs_times)
) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, arm), by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame", keep = "arm"))
```

```{r fig1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Simulated PQ and CPQ profiles by dose arm (median and 5th-95th percentiles of the individual predictions, 200 virtual children per arm). Compare with the observed data of Figure 1 and the VPC of Figure 3."}
vpc <- sim |>
  filter(time <= 72) |>
  select(id, arm, time, PQ = Cc, CPQ = Cc_cpq) |>
  pivot_longer(c(PQ, CPQ), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, levels = c("PQ", "CPQ"))) |>
  group_by(arm, analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ arm, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after primaquine (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

Table 3 reports Cmax, Tmax and AUC0-inf from the empirical Bayes estimates,
i.e. from individual predictions without residual error. PKNCA is applied to
the simulated individual predictions `Cc` and `Cc_cpq` in the same way.

```{r pknca}
nca_input <- sim |>
  select(id, arm, time, PQ = Cc, CPQ = Cc_cpq) |>
  pivot_longer(c(PQ, CPQ), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc))
stopifnot(all(nca_input$conc >= -1e-6 * max(nca_input$conc)))
# Floor the integrator undershoot and drop the numerically-zero post-peak
# tail (PQ falls below 1e-6 of its peak within a week in fast metabolizers),
# so the half-life fit does not follow integrator noise.
nca_input <- nca_input |>
  mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0)) |>
  group_by(id, analyte) |>
  filter(time <= time[which.max(conc)] | conc >= 1e-4 * max(conc)) |>
  ungroup()

dose_df <- ev |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, arm, time, amt) |>
  tidyr::crossing(analyte = c("PQ", "CPQ"))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_input, conc ~ time | arm + analyte + id,
  concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h"
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + analyte + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(nca_tab$PPORRES))
nca_tab |>
  group_by(analyte, arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(PPORRES), p05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05), p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Analyte" = analyte, "Arm" = arm, "Parameter" = PPTESTCD,
    "Median" = median, "5th pct" = p05, "95th pct" = p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated NCA, 200 virtual children per arm.")
```

# Comparison against Table 3

Table 3 summarises by the median, which `ncaComparisonTable()` also uses for
the simulated per-subject values.

```{r table3}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~arm,         ~tmax, ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,
  "PQ",  "0.25 mg/kg", 1.6,  50.2,  450.4,
  "CPQ", "0.25 mg/kg", 7.1, 108.3, 2912.3,
  "PQ",  "0.40 mg/kg", 1.6,  88.9,  730.7,
  "CPQ", "0.40 mg/kg", 6.6, 196.8, 5091.7
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_tab |> select(analyte, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  reference = published,
  by = c("analyte", "arm"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated median vs Goncalves 2017 Table 3 median.")

sim_med <- nca_tab |>
  group_by(analyte, arm, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
chk <- published |>
  pivot_longer(c(tmax, cmax, aucinf.obs), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pub") |>
  left_join(sim_med, by = c("analyte", "arm", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / pub - 1))
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed clearance, F50, dose or the molar ratio
  # shifts every exposure row by tens of percent.
  abs(median(chk$pct_diff[chk$PPTESTCD != "tmax"])) < 15,
  # Envelope over all exposure rows: Table 3 summarises 18 and 20 children,
  # so its medians carry roughly +/- 15-20% sampling error of their own.
  all(abs(chk$pct_diff[chk$PPTESTCD != "tmax"]) < 35)
)
```

PQ Cmax, Tmax and AUC agree with Table 3 to within 6%. The CPQ
AUC is lower than Table 3 by a similar fraction in both arms. CPQ exposure
depends on the fraction of PQ cleared by MAO, and so on the distribution of
activity scores, which the paper reports only in groups (see Virtual cohort).
It would also be raised by the less-than-linear CYP2D6 effect that Figure 5
suggests above AS 1 (see Assumptions). The Table 3 medians summarise only 18
and 20 children, with a between-subject spread in CPQ AUC of about fivefold,
so a median carries a sampling error of roughly 15%. The model parameters
were not adjusted.

## AUC against body weight (Figure 4)

Figure 4 shows that, although the dose is scaled linearly with weight, AUC
rises with weight. The model reproduces this through the 0.75 allometric
exponent on clearance and the age-maturation of F.

```{r fig4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Simulated AUC0-inf against body weight by arm. Compare Figure 4 of Goncalves 2017."}
auc_wt <- nca_tab |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, WT), by = "id")
ggplot(auc_wt, aes(WT, PPORRES, colour = arm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(analyte, levels = c("PQ", "CPQ")), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Body weight (kg)", y = "AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
slopes <- auc_wt |>
  group_by(analyte, arm) |>
  summarise(r = cor(log(WT), log(PPORRES), method = "spearman"), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(slopes$r > 0.2))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Liver volume.** The paper computes VL from weight and height with
  Johnson 2005, which is not open access. Its abstract gives
  `VL (L) = 0.722 * BSA^1.176`; the BSA formula is not stated in Goncalves
  2017. The packaged model uses the DuBois (< 15 kg) / Haycock (>= 15 kg)
  pair that `Brussee_2018b_midazolam_children_pbpk` uses with the same
  liver-volume equation. Halving or doubling VL changes Cmax by less than 2%
  (above), so the choice does not affect the plasma predictions.
* **Hepatic extraction ratio.** The Methods define `EH = CLint/(QH + CLint)`
  and `CLH = EH * QH` without stating whether `CLint` is the sum of the
  pathways. The packaged model uses the summed `CLint` (the standard
  well-stirred form, in which liver outflow totals QH). Computing a separate
  extraction ratio per pathway lowers the AS 1 PQ concentration at 12 h by
  12% relative to Figure 5 panel C, while the summed form reproduces it to
  within 1%.
* **CYP2D6 effect at AS 2 and 3.** The Methods specify a linear effect,
  `CLint,CYP2D6,i = AS * CLint,CYP2D6,pop`, and the model uses it. The AS 2
  and AS 3 curves of Figure 5 correspond to effective activity scores of
  about 1.82 and 2.47 under that equation, while the AS 0 and AS 1 curves match
  to within the digitising error. The figure appears to have been drawn with a less-than-linear CYP2D6
  effect above AS 1. The printed equation was kept. Only three ultrarapid
  metabolizers (AS 3) were in the study.
* **Between-subject variability scale.** Table 2 prints the IIV as a
  percentage under an exponential model. It is read as a log-normal CV and
  converted with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` (0.523 for VPQ and 0.355 for
  CLint,MAO). Reading it as `100 * omega` would give 0.687 and 0.426. Nothing
  in the paper settles this. The typical-value checks above do not depend on
  it.
* **Residual error.** The additive component is fixed at 2 ng/mL (half the
  LLOQ, M6 method), printed in ng/mL although the fit was molar. The packaged
  model keeps it in ng/mL.
* **Molar conversion.** The paper fitted molar concentrations and reported
  ng/mL. Molecular weights are not printed. 259.35 g/mol (PQ base,
  C15H21N3O) and 274.32 g/mol (CPQ, C15H18N2O3) are consistent with the
  paper's monitored [M+H]+ ions of 260.30 and 275.25 m/z. The 2-year-old and
  14-year-old CPQ curves of Figure 5 are reproduced to within 1%.
* **QH scaling.** QH (49.5 L/h at 70 kg) is scaled with the 0.75 exponent, as
  the Methods state for all flows. The Figure 5 PQ peaks are reproduced
  to within 1%; leaving QH unscaled would raise the 14-year-old PQ peak by about
  7%.
* **Virtual cohort.** Age, weight and height distributions and the split of
  the intermediate and extensive CYP2D6 groups into activity scores are
  assumptions built from the Table 1 medians and IQRs (see Virtual cohort).
  The Figure 5 children have no stated heights; 85 cm and 151 cm are used.
* **Co-medication.** Primaquine was given with artemether-lumefantrine, and
  lumefantrine inhibits CYP2D6 in vitro (Discussion). The estimated CYP2D6
  clearance therefore applies to that co-administration.
